stem: A convex mirror used for rear-view on an automobile has a radius of curvature of 3.00 m. If a bus is located at 5.00 m from this mirror, find the position, nature and size of the image.
solution:
**Given.** \(R = +3.00\) m (the principal focus of a convex mirror is behind it), \(u = -5.00\) m.

**Focal length.**

\(f = R/2 = +1.50\) m

**Image position.**

\(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{1.50} - \dfrac{1}{-5.00} = \dfrac{1}{1.50} + \dfrac{1}{5.00} = \dfrac{6.50}{7.50}\)

\(v = +1.15\) m

The positive sign puts the image **1.15 m behind the mirror**.

**Magnification.**

\(m = -\dfrac{v}{u} = -\dfrac{1.15}{-5.00} = +0.23\)

**Nature.** The image is **virtual, erect and diminished**, smaller by a factor of 0.23 — which is exactly what a rear-view mirror is for.
groundedIn: §9.2.4 Mirror Formula and Magnification, which gives \(1/v + 1/u = 1/f\) and \(m = h'/h = -v/u\), with §9.2.3 Sign Convention for Reflection by Spherical Mirrors for the New Cartesian signs.

stem: An object, 4.0 cm in size, is placed at 25.0 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15.0 cm. At what distance from the mirror should a screen be placed in order to obtain a sharp image? Find the nature and the size of the image.
solution:
**Given.** \(h = +4.0\) cm, \(u = -25.0\) cm, \(f = -15.0\) cm (concave).

**Image position.**

\(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{-15.0} - \dfrac{1}{-25.0} = \dfrac{-5.0 + 3.0}{75.0} = \dfrac{-2.0}{75.0}\)

\(v = -37.5\) cm

The negative sign puts the image **in front of the mirror**, so the screen should be placed **37.5 cm in front of the mirror**. An image that can be caught on a screen is **real**.

**Size.**

\(m = \dfrac{h'}{h} = -\dfrac{v}{u}\), so \(h' = -\dfrac{v\,h}{u} = -\dfrac{(-37.5)(+4.0)}{(-25.0)} = -6.0\) cm

**Nature.** The image is **real, inverted** (the negative \(h'\)) and **enlarged** — 6.0 cm against an object of 4.0 cm.
groundedIn: §9.2.4 Mirror Formula and Magnification, which gives \(1/v + 1/u = 1/f\) and \(m = h'/h = -v/u\), with §9.2.3 Sign Convention for Reflection by Spherical Mirrors for the New Cartesian signs.

subtopic: Lens Formula and Power of a Lens
stem: A concave lens has focal length of 15 cm. At what distance should the object from the lens be placed so that it forms an image at 10 cm from the lens? Also, find the magnification produced by the lens.
solution:
**Given.** \(f = -15\) cm (concave). A concave lens always forms a **virtual, erect image on the same side as the object**, so \(v = -10\) cm.

**Object position.**

\(\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}\), so \(\dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{-10} - \dfrac{1}{-15} = \dfrac{-3 + 2}{30} = \dfrac{-1}{30}\)

\(u = -30\) cm

The object is **30 cm from the lens**.

**Magnification.**

\(m = \dfrac{v}{u} = \dfrac{-10}{-30} = +\dfrac{1}{3} = +0.33\)

The positive sign shows the image is **erect and virtual**, and it is **one-third the size of the object**.

Reading the sign of \(v\) off the physics rather than guessing it is the whole difficulty here: a concave lens cannot form a real image, so \(v\) had to be negative.
groundedIn: §9.3.7 Lens Formula and Magnification, which gives \(1/v - 1/u = 1/f\) and \(m = h'/h = v/u\), with §9.3.6 Sign Convention for Spherical Lenses.

subtopic: Lens Formula and Power of a Lens
stem: A 2.0 cm tall object is placed perpendicular to the principal axis of a convex lens of focal length 10 cm. The distance of the object from the lens is 15 cm. Find the nature, position and size of the image. Also find its magnification.
solution:
**Given.** \(h = +2.0\) cm, \(f = +10\) cm (convex), \(u = -15\) cm.

**Image position.**

\(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{-15} = \dfrac{3 - 2}{30} = \dfrac{1}{30}\)

\(v = +30\) cm

The positive sign puts the image **30 cm on the other side of the lens**, so it is **real**.

**Magnification and size.**

\(m = \dfrac{v}{u} = \dfrac{30}{-15} = -2\)

\(h' = m\,h = -2 \times 2.0 = -4.0\) cm

**Nature.** The image is **real, inverted** (the negative signs) and **enlarged to twice the object's size** — 4.0 cm tall, 30 cm from the lens on the far side.

The object at 15 cm lies between \(f\) and \(2f\), which is exactly the range that gives a real, inverted, magnified image.
groundedIn: §9.3.7 Lens Formula and Magnification, which gives \(1/v - 1/u = 1/f\) and \(m = h'/h = v/u\), with §9.3.6 Sign Convention for Spherical Lenses.
